analysis:
PORTFOLIO REVIEW (Aug 12, 2026): The book is effectively full at 94% deployment with only $1,055 of gross-cap headroom remaining — far too little to size any meaningful new position. Adding a position of $1,055 would be a rounding error and violate the spirit of the 1–2% equity-at-risk rule. No trades today.

EXISTING POSITIONS: A (+15.25%) is the standout winner — thesis intact (quality analytical instrumentation, strong FCF), no reason to exit early. AMP (+4.65%) and LMT (+4.53%) are progressing normally; both are quality businesses in mild uptrends. MCO (+1.13%) and TEL (+1.68%) are barely off cost — no thesis breaks visible, just slow movers. Portfolio heat is only 1.88% despite near-full deployment, which reflects relatively tight stops and quality names not in distress.

PERFORMANCE HONESTY: Profit factor 0.55x and Sortino -1.60 are poor. The three WDAY stop-outs show the real cost of forced entries; the two FDS wins show what patient, high-conviction setups can do. The lesson is clear: wait for the Weinstein Stage 1→2 transition with proper sizing capacity, not just a quality screen pass.

CANDIDATE SCAN: Several interesting names exist (ADBE at fair valuation with strong FCF; BRO with accelerating revenue; CRM with compelling fwd P/E of 12.7x) but CRM reports in 14 days and ADBE in 29 days — entering ahead of catalysts that could gap either way is speculation, not edge. IT is 24.8% above SMA50 — extended late-cycle entry. FDS, which we traded profitably twice, is now 12.5% above SMA50 and 15% above SMA200 with earnings in 36 days — not a fresh basing setup. No candidate clears both the asymmetric setup AND the sizing capacity hurdle simultaneously.

ACTION: Hold all five positions. Let A run toward its prior range highs. Keep stops current on MCO and TEL. Cash is the sixth position today. Revisit if A or another position hits target or stop, freeing capacity for a properly sized new entry.
